attempts.paper_title: Diversification of dentate gyrus granule cell subtypes is regulated by Nrg1 nuclear back-signaling
attempts.entry_title: Dentate granule cell subtypes and the Nrg1 V321L mutation (Rajebhosale et al. 2025)
attempts.summary: Only the finding that granule and semilunar cells lose their electrical differences in the V321L mutant held in these recordings. The wild-type differences in resting potential, spike width and downstroke went the paper's way but were not significant (p = 0.08 to 0.35), and the separation of wild-type cell types by PCA and a trained classifier also failed. The morphology, soma position, Golgi and RNAScope findings could not be tested because those data are not in the dandiset. The sequencing findings on Penk+ cells and pseudotime could not be tested either, because the kept nuclei and cluster labels are not deposited and the pipeline needs R. The embryonic expression of the semilunar-cell genes held, judged by eye on Allen atlas images.
attempts.description: Tests the electrophysiological findings of Rajebhosale et al. (2025) on dandiset 001545, which holds whole-cell current clamp recordings of 48 dentate granule cells (GCs and semilunar granule cells) from 5 wild-type and 5 Nrg1 V321L mice. It compares the resting potential and spike shape of the two cell types in each genotype and repeats the paper's LDA, k-means, PCA and classifier analyses. Soma positions, morphology, histology and the snMultiome data are not in the dandiset.

On the 18 z-scored features (a) the WT GC mean LD1 is 1.97 and the other groups -1.43 to -0.33, and spike width has the largest LD1 coefficient (3.01, then downstroke -2.88), as the paper says. On the top 9 PCs (b) WT SGC is the group apart (1.67, the others -0.74 to -0.26) and the largest coefficients mapped back to the features are spike amplitude, AHP amplitude and sag (-0.48 to -0.43). Question for the paper's authors (recorded as a methods_unavailable finding). Was the four-class LDA of Fig 2M fitted on the z-scored features or on PCs, as the classifier of Fig S2G is? The Methods' LDA section describes only the classifier (scale, prcomp, top 9 PCs, caret lda).

outcomes.statement: In the WT-trained LDA, the distance between GC and SGC centroids along LD1 is much smaller in V321L than in WT, with both V321L centroids on the WT SGC side of the boundary.
outcomes.source: Figure S2F; Results, V321L mutation in Nrg1 results in altered composition of the DG granule cell population, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: Centroid analysis demonstrated a striking reduction in the separation between GC and SGC centroids in V 321 L mice along the first linear discriminant (LD1) axis
outcomes.notes: WT centroids on LD1 GC -0.87, SGC 1.31 (distance 2.18), boundary 0.40. V321L centroids GC -0.10 and SGC 0.07 with their own scaling (distance 0.17, 0.08 of WT), or -0.47 and -0.17 with the WT scaling (0.30, 0.14 of WT). The distance condition holds; both V321L centroids lie on the WT GC side of the boundary, and of the midpoint boundary (0.22), so the side condition does not. The criterion requires both conditions and gives no partial rule, so the outcome is not reproduced (changed from partially reproduced after verification). The criterion rests on the paper's R pipeline (Seurat with scDblFinder doublet removal, harmony integration, clustering over 41 resolutions and a hand-curated merge into final clusters, Rcode_20230522.txt in RajNINDS/V321L-snMultiome at c124726), whose packages cannot be installed in this entry's locked Python environment. The nuclei it kept and its cluster labels (the GC clusters 0, 1, 5 and 18) are not deposited, so a Python re-analysis would substitute its own cell calling and clustering for the paper's. Not attempted.

outcomes.statement: In ATAC space the Penk+ GCs (cluster 9) have the maximal pseudotime; WT GC trajectories have three end points and V321L GC trajectories one, ending at cluster 9.
outcomes.source: Figure S8A; Results, Non-SGCs harbor the potential to express an SGC-like transcriptomic state, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Once again, we found that the Penk + GCs (now located in ATAC cluster 9) had the maximum pseudotime values based on chromatin accessibility ... However, in the V 321 L GCs, there was only one end point terminating at cluster 9
outcomes.notes: Needs per-nucleus ATAC fragments (the Methods import atac_fragments.tsv.gz into Signac). GEO holds only a smoothed cut-site track per sample and per-barcode peak counts in the raw matrices; the fragments would have to be regenerated from the raw reads with Cell Ranger ARC, and the analysis needs Signac and Monocle3 (R), which cannot be installed in this entry's locked Python environment. Not attempted. The criterion's parenthesis called the LL samples WT and VV V321L, while the GEO sample records and the dandiset say VV is the wild type; this was asked of a reader in questions/001545.yaml. The reader amended the criterion to WT (VV) and V321L (LL), citing the snMultiome code, which merges the VV samples as project WT. The statement and expected values are unchanged. The answer does not bear on the block (no fragments, and R tools outside the locked environment), so the claim stays blocked as before; a later attempt that can run it should take VV as WT.

outcomes.statement: At E18.5, cells expressing SGC-enriched genes (Penk, Scg2, Nrg1, Cit) lie at the dorsal border of the developing GCL, so marker expression is unlikely to reflect cellular age alone.
outcomes.source: Figure S9C; Results, SGC numbers in the DG increase during the adolescence-adulthood transition in WT mice, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: We found cells expressing SGC-enriched genes such as Penk , Scg2 , Nrg1 , and Cit in the dorsal border of the developing GCL at E18.5
outcomes.notes: Tested after verification (it was blocked as other, not attempted). The Allen Developing Mouse Brain Atlas holds one E18.5 ISH series per gene, all sagittal (Penk 100055886, Scg2 100083699, Nrg1 100057764, Cit 100077439). The criterion is a reading of the images by eye. Penk labels a band of cells along the dorsal (outer) edge of the dentate crescent in all three sections shown (45, 52, 59), and Nrg1 a dense band along the same edge (26, 33, 47). The atlas alignment puts the Scg2 crops off the crescent, so its two sections (29, 43) are also shown recentred by eye on their own crescent. There section 43 shows a band of labelled cells along the dorsal edge and section 29 a faint band with a few labelled cells; the expression mask covers 0.0032 and 0.0010 of the recentred crops (0.0008 in the off-centre section 29 crop), against 0.0123 for Penk and 0.0072 for Nrg1. Scg2 labels other regions strongly (whole-brain expression density 0.043). Cit (27, 41, 48) shows sparse, faint labelled cells along that edge (mask 0.0007). The criterion has one condition, labelled cells at the dorsal border for each of the four genes, and no partial rule, as for figs2f; all four meet it, Scg2 and Cit faintly, so the outcome is reproduced (changed from partially reproduced in round 3). The outcome rests on locating the dentate gyrus by eye, as the atlas does not annotate it at E18.5, and on a judgement by eye. Which images Fig S9C shows is asked of the paper's authors (methods_unavailable finding).
deviations: The Allen data are identified by their section data set ids and read through the Allen API; they have no DOI or versioned release to pin.

Assumed. The dentate gyrus is located by eye on Penk section 52 (image 101094568, pixel 3200, 2080), mapped to the E18.5 reference with the atlas's image_to_reference service and from there to each series with reference_to_image; the E18.5 annotation draws only the medial pallium, so no annotated location exists. The overviews in the notebook show where each crop lies. For Scg2 the alignment lands off the crescent, so its sections 29 and 43 are also cropped at a centre placed by eye on their own crescent (pixels 3450, 1900 and 3330, 1730).

Three sections per gene are shown, those nearest the dentate point and 150 um to either side, at 2 um per pixel, and the middle one at full resolution with the atlas's expression mask (display choices).
outcomes.where: Allen Brain Atlas, developing mouse brain ISH at E18.5 (the paper names no experiment IDs)

findings.statement: The dandiset holds only the current clamp recordings. The soma positions and the morphology from the biocytin fills (splay angle, branch points, dendritic length, 15 parameters), on which Fig 1F to I, Fig 2C to H, Fig S1 and the multiple regression rest, are not in it, and neither are the Golgi and RNAScope data; 23 of the paper's 56 claims cannot be tested for this reason.

The files hold 13 WT GCs and 9 WT SGCs, where the paper's electrophysiology has 14 and 9, and 12 V321L GCs and 14 V321L SGCs, where the paper has 10 and 15. Nothing in the files says which WT GC is missing or why the V321L cell types differ, so the paper's cell sets cannot be rebuilt.
Every CurrentClampStimulusSeries stores the current in picoamperes (values -60 to 300) under the unit amperes with conversion 1.
The electrode cell_id is VP neuron in all 48 files, though the cells are dentate granule cells.

The general stimulus field says neurons were kept near -65 mV with a constant current and stepped from -60 to 200 pA. The voltage before the steps is -68 to -89 mV in every cell, 14 cells were stepped to 250 or 300 pA, and the bias_current attribute is 10 pA in every sweep, so whether a holding current was applied, and how much, cannot be told. Every sweep of every file also stores the same bridge balance (20 MOhm) and capacitance compensation (1 pF), which look like defaults.

The genotype is coded only as VV or LL in the subject ids; the surgery field says VV is wild type and LL the valine-to-leucine mutant, and GEO agrees, but the cell type is given only as the end of the session description (semilunar or not semilunar), with no column or field of its own.

Question for the paper's authors. Was the four-class LDA of Fig 2M and Fig S2C fitted on the z-scored features or on principal components, as the classifier of Fig S2G is? The Methods' LDA section describes only the classifier. On this dandiset the two give different groups apart on LD1 (WT GC on the features, WT SGC on 9 PCs).

Question for the paper's authors. Which twenty features were extracted, and how were cells with a missing feature handled in the LDA, k-means and PCA? The Methods cite Kim et al (2024), Fig S2C lists eighteen, and the linked code returns twenty-one. Here 4 cells lack the code's AHP width and were dropped, which fits the 21 WT and 23 V321L cells of the Fig S2G matrices.

Question for the paper's authors. Which Allen Developing Mouse Brain ISH series and sections does Fig S9C show for Penk, Scg2, Nrg1 and Cit at E18.5? The atlas holds one sagittal E18.5 series per gene; in those, Penk and Nrg1 label cells along the dorsal edge of the dentate crescent clearly, and Scg2 and Cit only faintly.

GEO GSE280167, where the paper deposited the snMultiome data, holds the raw feature-barcode matrix of every barcode per mouse (genes and peaks) and a smoothed ATAC cut-site track per sample. The nuclei kept after filtering and doublet removal, the cluster labels the paper's snRNA-Seq figures rest on, and the per-nucleus ATAC fragments are not deposited.

entries.title: Dentate granule cell subtypes and the Nrg1 V321L mutation (Rajebhosale et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the electrophysiological findings of Rajebhosale et al. (2025) on dandiset 001545, which holds whole-cell current clamp recordings of 48 dentate granule cells (GCs and semilunar granule cells) from 5 wild-type and 5 Nrg1 V321L mice. It compares the resting potential and spike shape of the two cell types in each genotype and repeats the paper's LDA, k-means, PCA and classifier analyses. Soma positions, morphology, histology and the snMultiome data are not in the dandiset.
